title: What is known about 1RB1RE_0RC0RF_1LC1RD_1RA0LE_0RA0LD_0RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_0RC0RF_1LC1RD_1RA0LE_0RA0LD_0RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of blocks of a = 111110 and b = 111010. In each phase one block of a's is moved into another, one a at a time, while a block of b's grows; when it runs out the blocks are reorganised, several levels deep. Only the shape is known, from simulation; one sweep rule is proved in Lean. No halt in 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 59,841 cells have been visited and 43,359 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.07). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493).

claims.title: The sweep over the b-block
claims.text: L 0 A> b^n R → L (010111)^n 0 A> R in 10n steps: the block is crossed unchanged, for all n and any tapes around.

claims.title: Phases, observed
claims.text: From step 8.3·108 to 109 the tape is 1^2 0 a^7 1^3 0 1^2 0 a^x 1^3 0 1^2 0 a^y b a b a b^2 a^5 b^5 a b^z ... with x + y = 7388 fixed and z = x − 3716: one a moves from a^y to a^x, and b^z gains one, about every 6 new cells on the right. Earlier phases show the same pattern with more levels. Seen in simulation, not proved.

claims.title: Where it would halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is F reading 1, and F is entered only from B reading 1, so the machine halts exactly when the head in state B reads 1 1 (from the transition table).

claims.title: Size of the tape description (family screen)
claims.text: At the 8 records between 2.6·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.7·10<sup>10</sup> steps (first new leftmost or rightmost cell after each threshold 10<sup>6</sup>·4^k) the tape has 28,120 to 265,812 visited cells and compresses to 8 to 35 level-2 tokens (repeats of a word of at most 40 cells, then repeats of groups of such tokens).

claims.title: No halt in the first 7·10<sup>16</sup> steps
claims.text: The macro simulator of the family screen (blocks of 6 cells, runs of one word crossed at once, exact, checked against the direct simulator) runs from blank tape past step 7·10<sup>16</sup> without a halt.

claims.title: Proposed family: F01, periodic blocks driven by a bounded engine
claims.text: The description is small: 8 to 35 level-2 tokens at every record from 2.6·108 to 1.7·1010 steps, and 13 to 38 runs in the macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells) at the sampled records from 106 to 7·1016 steps. For example at step 5·1012 the macro tape is 000110 (111110)^130829 111011 (011111)^354778 011100 (101110)^52876 111010 (101110)^59089 and 12 more six-cell words. A few long periodic blocks that are transferred into one another, with a short tail, is the F01 shape. The number of blocks changes with the phase (between 3 and 7 long blocks at the sampled records above 1012 steps) but did not grow.

claims.title: Eras of bouncer passes, growing by factors 1, 6 and 16
claims.text: Observed up to 10<sup>16</sup> steps: the run is a sequence of eras. In an era a wall of one word grows by one block per sweep and eats a run of n blocks while another run grows at the far end, a few passes of about n sweeps each. Two kinds of era alternate, and the main run has 7,389, 7,401, 118,265, 118,281, 709,541 and 4,257,168 blocks at the starts of the last six eras: factors of about 1, 16, 1, 6 and 6. The factor is decided between the passes by the short markers and the irregular tail at the right end; that rule is not known.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Only the shape of the run is known; the phase rules and the reorganisation between phases are not found (see "For later" in the README).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine keeps a list of blocks made of two words, a = 111110 and b = 111010, and moves one block into another, one word at a time, while a third block grows. When a block runs out the list is reorganised. The shape is clear from simulation; the rules are still to be decoded.

facts.text: No halt in the macro simulator.
Within a phase one a-block feeds another.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Blocks feeding blocks
html: With a = 111110 and b = 111010, at each new cell on the right the tape looks like
11 0 a^7 1110 11 0 a^x 1110 11 0 a^y b a b a bb a^5 b^5 a b^z [right end]

From step 8.3·108 to 109, x + y = 7388 stays fixed while x grows from 4632 to 6231 and z = x − 3716 grows with it: one a moves from the third block to the second, and the b-block gains one, about every six new cells at the right end. The right end itself changes at every step like a small counter.

Earlier phases look the same with more levels, for example 11 0 a^5 1110 11 0 a^632 1110 1110 1110 a^u 1110 11 0 a^v bb a b a b aa b^w with u + v constant from step 2.1·107 to 3.0·107. When the feeding block runs out the list is reorganised and a new phase begins.

sections.heading: Open
html: The machine halts exactly when the head in state B reads 1 1. Whether a reorganisation can produce that depends on rules that have not been found yet.

sections.heading: Eras: a few bouncer passes, then a jump in size
html: Followed for 1016 steps and read in blocks of six cells, the run falls into eras. An era starts when the head turns at the left end of the tape with no long run behind it. Everything in this section is observed in one run. None of it is proved.

Inside an era the machine is a bouncer. A wall of one word grows by one block per sweep and eats a run of n blocks, while a new run grows at the far end; one such pass takes about n sweeps, and an era has a few passes. For example, in the era that starts at step 301,992,023,962 a wall of 110111 grows from 332 to 117,663 blocks in 117,332 sweeps while a run of 100000 shrinks from 117,946 to 615.

From one era to the next the main run grows by a factor that is not constant: about 1, 16, 1, 6 and 6 for the last six eras. The short markers between the runs and an irregular tail of about a dozen blocks at the right end, which changes at every sweep, decide it. The rule for that is the missing piece: with it, the whole run would be a map from one era to the next.

sections.heading: Which family it belongs to
html: The 22 machines of family F09 (“bouncers over lists of counters, not yet classified”) were screened in one way. The machine runs from blank tape for 2·1010 steps; each time the tape reaches a new cell after a threshold, the tape is compressed twice: first repeats of one word, then repeats of groups of words. If the tape is a few growing blocks and a bounded rest, the number of level-2 tokens stays bounded while the tape grows. Everything in this section is observed in one run. None of it is proved.

Proposed family: F01, periodic blocks driven by a bounded engine (three to six long blocks of period-6 words and a short tail).

The description is small: 8 to 35 level-2 tokens at every record from 2.6·108 to 1.7·1010 steps, and 13 to 38 runs in the macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells) at the sampled records from 106 to 7·1016 steps. For example at step 5·1012 the macro tape is 000110 (111110)^130829 111011 (011111)^354778 011100 (101110)^52876 111010 (101110)^59089 and 12 more six-cell words.

A few long periodic blocks that are transferred into one another, with a short tail, is the F01 shape. The number of blocks changes with the phase (between 3 and 7 long blocks at the sampled records above 1012 steps) but did not grow.
Next step. Sample at the records where the tape is shortest (state D at the left end) and find the map on the block lengths and the tail; then the F01 closure.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.07). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493).
After 109 steps the tape spans 59,841 cells (17 left of the start, 39,070 right), with a density of 1s of 0.725.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Eras of bouncer passes over a few long runs; the main run grows by factors of about 1, 6 or 16 from era to era, decided by short markers and an irregular tail at the right end; no halt in 7·10^16 steps; era map not found.
